ai-agent: A single wide horizontal panel. Down the far left edge runs a narrow grey strip where a chatbot icon takes in a question mark and emits one short sentence that dead-ends at a stop sign — one reply, then silence. The rest of the frame belongs to the agent: a small robot walking a long, winding trail through a messy landscape of bogs, boulders and one collapsed bridge, beneath a sun that arcs from dawn to dusk to show that the work lasts hours. It never lets go of the rolled blueprint it carries, stamped GOAL: BUILD THIS WEBSITE — a destination flag, not a question — and from its belt hang its tools, drawn literally: a terminal window, a browser window, and a magnifying lens for viewing images. Stone waymarkers repeat along the trail in an unbroken loop reading PLAN, ACT, CHECK, CORRECT. At the collapsed bridge the path visibly doubles back before a detour is found, recovering from failure; midway, the robot pauses to study a screenshot of its own half-built site, a red flaw circled on it, an arrow curving back along the trail to fix what it has seen. The trail ends at a gleaming, finished website on a plinth beside a stack of coins — the long, messy, multi-step journey being what valuable work actually looks like — while beyond the end flag the path continues faintly toward a glowing horizon, where tiny figures of engineers are still laying paving stones at the frontier of AI development.
distillation: A tall, ornate glass vessel shaped like a human head — labeled "TEACHER" and glowing with dense, intricate patterns of light inside — pours a thin luminous stream through a funnel into a much smaller, simpler vessel labeled "STUDENT," whose interior is filling with the same swirling patterns but coarser and fainter, showing how a big model's ability is compressed into a small one that punches above its size; yet the stream itself is the object of dispute, for a translucent legal contract floats beside the teacher vessel, half of it stamped with a padlock and the words "OUTPUTS — NO TRAINING" while the other half is torn away, and in the background a mirror shows the teacher vessel itself being filled from a firehose spraying pages, books, and websites harvested from an endless public web, with no permission asked; between the two vessels, two groups of tiny silhouetted figures face each other across the flowing stream — one gesturing angrily at the lock, the other pointing back at the mirror — while beneath the whole scene a floor of shifting, half-melted tiles spells out the word "UNRESOLVED," making clear that the picture's real subject is not the transfer of knowledge but the still-unsettled fight over whether one model learning from another differs at all from learning from the internet.
mixture-of-experts: An illustration of a vast, luminous neural network rendered as a towering hospital-like structure of the mind: hundreds of small, distinct "expert" chambers — each labeled with a specialty such as mathematics, languages, history, code — arranged in stacked rows and mostly dim and dormant in cool grey. At the entrance, a glowing gatekeeper figure (the router) reads an incoming scroll of text and throws a handful of bright switches, causing only two or three chambers to light up in warm gold, sending their signals forward along a few lit pathways while the rest of the immense network stays dark. Beside the scene, a simple ledger graphic contrasts the full mountain of the network's total knowledge with the tiny lit fraction drawn upon at this moment, with a caption reading: "Trillions of parameters known; only a few consulted — the whole hospital's wisdom, but only the specialists you need."
open-weights: A wide, split-panel illustration showing a colossal, translucent cube made of countless tiny glowing numbers hovering in the center, like a three-dimensional spreadsheet. From the left, a tall corporate tower with locked doors and a toll booth extends a tethered cable toward the cube, with users lining up to access it through a guarded terminal. From the right, the cube's numerical contents pour downward like a waterfall of digits into an open shipping crate beside an ordinary person's home workstation, where the same cube — an identical copy — floats above a personal computer, complete and unbound. Inside the home scene, small details carry the entry's tensions: a robust-looking GPU rack hinting at the hardware needed to run the copy; a hand reaching into the cube to pluck out and rearrange digits, showing it can be modified; a padlock icon visibly detaching from the copied cube, signaling that built-in safeguards can be stripped away; and behind everything, a stylized one-way turnstile door through which the numbers have passed and can never return, rendered in bold red as the image's focal warning. A caption-like banner across the bottom distinguishes the two halves: on the tower side, "closed: rules and prices"; on the home side, "open weights: download, run, change — no going back."
